title: Chicken Pot Pie
description: chicken, mushroom and vegetable filling with a pastry lid. Dinner for the two of us.
imageAlt: Reference photograph: Golden, flaky chicken pot pie cut open on a white plate, with a softly blurred background.
imageCaption: Reference photograph · chicken pot-pie variation · displayed crop
personalNote: Keep stirring while the water goes in and we’ll get that nice, gooey filling. Use whichever flour we have in the cupboard.
equipment: Pan or wok safe in the oven at 180°C
advancePrep: Get everything chopped, boil 1 litre of water and preheat the oven to 180°C. Have the pastry sheet ready according to its packet.
importantNotes: This makes two portions for dinner. Check that the pan or wok, including its handles, is safe to put in the oven. We can use plain/all-purpose flour or self-raising flour. If we use cornflour instead, mix it with a little cold water and stir it into the hot stock rather than roasting it dry.

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.note: Or use 3 smaller carrots. Peel and dice.

ingredients.name: Bay leaves
ingredients.note: We take these out before serving or adding pastry.

ingredients.name: Dried thyme
ingredients.note: Don’t worry if we don’t have any.

ingredients.name: Green peas
ingredients.note: Add at the end. If frozen, let them thaw or cook as the packet says first.

groups.title: To thicken the filling and give it a lid

ingredients.name: Plain or all-purpose flour
ingredients.note: Self-raising flour is fine too. If we have neither, use 1 tablespoon of cornflour instead.

ingredients.name: Cold water for cornflour
ingredients.note: Only if using cornflour: a little to mix it into a smooth paste.

ingredients.name: Pastry sheet
ingredients.note: Enough to cover the pan as well as possible. Follow the packet’s handling instructions.

steps.title: Get everything ready
steps.description: Chop the chicken breast into small pieces. Dice the brown onion, peel and dice the carrots, peel and dice the garlic, and slice the mushrooms. Boil the water for the stock. Put the oven on at 180°C too, so it’s ready when we need it.

steps.title: Start with the chicken
steps.description: Put the chicken into the oven-safe pan or wok on medium-high heat and fry for about 5 minutes, until the outside turns white. Squish it around so it cooks evenly. This is just the first stage; it finishes cooking later.
steps.doneness: Chicken white on the outside; continue with the rest of the cooking.

steps.title: Soften the onion, garlic and carrots
steps.description: Add the onion, garlic and carrots. Squish them around with the chicken for another 10 minutes, until the vegetables soften. Keep moving them around so the garlic doesn’t catch.
steps.doneness: Onion and carrots beginning to soften.

steps.title: Add the mushrooms and the stock flavours
steps.description: Add the chicken stock cubes, bay leaves, optional dried thyme and sliced mushrooms. Cook for another 5 minutes, squishing everything around, until the mushrooms soften. If there’s no thyme in the cupboard, don’t worry about it.

steps.title: Stir in and cook the flour
steps.description: If we’re using plain/all-purpose or self-raising flour, add it now and mix it around with everything for 2 minutes. We’re cooking out the flour and giving it that slightly nutty taste. It’s what helps the filling become nice and gooey. If we’re using cornflour, skip the dry-flour stage and mix it with a little cold water in a cup instead; we add that after the stock.
steps.tip: Use this 2-minute timer for the wheat flour. Skip it for the cornflour paste.

steps.title: Add the hot water slowly
steps.description: Pour in the boiled water slowly, in three or four additions if that helps. Keep stirring as each bit goes in so the flour doesn’t go lumpy. If we’re using cornflour, add the hot water first, then stir the smooth cornflour paste into it and bring it back to a bubble.

steps.title: Let the filling cook down
steps.description: Let the filling bubble for another 10 minutes, stirring every minute or so and scraping the bottom so nothing burns. We want the sauce thick and gooey. If it still looks too loose to hold the pastry, let it reduce a little longer.
steps.doneness: Thick filling with fully cooked chicken.

steps.title: Peas and pepper, then take out the bay leaves
steps.description: Turn off the stove. Add the green peas and coarse ground black pepper, or pepper powder, and mix. Take out both bay leaves and throw them away.
steps.tip: If using frozen peas, thaw or cook them according to their packet first.

steps.title: Give the pie its pastry lid
steps.description: Lay the pastry sheet over the pan or wok and cover the top as well as you can. Make a small slit in the top for steam to escape. Don’t worry if it isn’t a perfectly neat lid.

steps.title: Bake and serve the pie
steps.description: Put the pan into the oven at 180°C and bake for about 40 minutes, until the pastry is golden and cooked and the filling is bubbling hot. Use oven gloves to take it out, and remember the handle stays hot. Serve straight away.
steps.doneness: Golden, cooked pastry and bubbling-hot filling.

substitutions.title: Whichever flour is in the cupboard
substitutions.text: For the two-portion pie, use 2 tablespoons of plain/all-purpose flour or self-raising flour. If we have neither, use 1 tablespoon of cornflour. The cornflour goes in as a cold-water paste after the hot stock, as written in the method.

troubleshooting.title: The filling is still a bit runny
troubleshooting.text: Give it a little longer to bubble before the pastry goes on, stirring and scraping the bottom. We want it thick enough to hold the pastry on top. Don’t spiral if it needs a few extra minutes.

troubleshooting.title: A few flour lumps
troubleshooting.text: Keep stirring and squash the lumps against the side of the pan. Adding the water slowly while stirring makes this much easier.

storage: If we have leftovers, cool them promptly and refrigerate within 1–2 hours. Eat within 48 hours or freeze.
reheating: Reheat once until the filling is steaming hot all the way through.
foodSafety: The first 5-minute fry only turns the outside of the chicken white. Check it is fully cooked before serving; a thermometer check is 75°C in the centre for 30 seconds.
servingSuggestion: Serve straight away, with a bit of that pastry and gooey filling on each plate.
